audit_name: Team A independent adversarial audit - security and healthcare patient data privacy

constraints: No source, git index/history, config, database, or sibling repository modification
No git add, commit, push, merge, network call, database access, or exploitation
No secrets or real patient data accessed or generated
Only artifacts under GOVERNANCE/ADVERSARIAL_ASSURANCE/ were written

methods: Read-only git status and git diff inspection
not_covered: Runtime exploitation or live request replay
Team C independent verification or certification
Modification or re-adjudication of owner-gated decisions
excluded_items: NR-011 FK test co-collection failure - already disclosed; not re-reported
backend/app/interoperability/fhir_http/security.py synthetic-header surface - reviewed but not counted as live because no factory include_router mount was found
GOVERNANCE/PUBLIC_ENDPOINT_REGISTER.md and owner decision records - treated as owner-gated evidence and left unchanged

observed_control_status.scope_note: One production endpoint only; otherwise NOT IMPLEMENTED

observed_control_status.control: Health Core authorization facade runtime wiring

summary.verdict: NOT CERTIFIED; release decision HOLD preserved

findings.title: NIAM governance, trust, lifecycle, federation, certificates and adaptive-auth control planes accept any authenticated actor

evidence.excerpt: _AUTH_REQUIRED = [Depends(get_current_niam_actor)]

governance, trust, lifecycle, federation, certificates, notifications, adaptive_auth, admin and compliance routers mounted with _AUTH_REQUIRED; professional_registry mounted without registry authorization dependency
stricter require_niam_registry_reader and require_niam_registry_writer exist but are applied only to persons, sessions and devices in router.py
POST /suspensions accepts caller-supplied suspended_by; no permission dependency
POST /registry/certify accepts caller-supplied verified_by, digital_signature and certification fields
POST /frameworks creates trust framework without permission dependency
POST /anchors creates trust anchor with caller-supplied key/certificate material
POST /federation creates federation trust relationship
POST /enterprise/{reg_id}/approve with caller-supplied approved_by
POST /providers registers identity provider including encrypted client secret field
certificate issue, revoke and rotate handlers have no permission dependency
POST /{registry_id}/verify uses verified_by=Depends(get_actor_identity_id)
get_actor_identity_id derives identity only; no role or authority check
verify is documented as the only privilege activation path; is_privileged is the single enforcement point

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Statically follow router.py:54-63 into any listed control-plane router; confirm only authentication is inherited and the handler mutates identity/trust/certificate/privilege state without an authorization dependency. Falsification requires an equivalent policy dependency as in access.py:59-75 or admin/routes.py:30-50 plus a negative test proving a non-privileged actor receives 403.
findings.root_cause: Authentication was treated as authorization for high-impact identity control planes; actor identity is used as an audit label rather than as input to an authorization decision.
findings.impact: Any authenticated NIAM identity can suspend identities, certify trust, register identity providers, issue or revoke certificates, and self-verify professional privilege entries, with downstream PHI and clinical authorization consequences.
findings.remediation: Apply explicit permission dependencies to every affected router and handler, derive all *_by fields from the authenticated principal, use AuthorizationDecisionService for mutations, and add negative authorization tests.
alternatives: Consolidate all NIAM control planes behind one gateway authorization dependency
Disable affected routers until role catalog and tests land
Keep router-level auth and add service-layer guardrails
findings.preferred_alternative: Consolidated gateway dependency plus handler-level defense in depth

findings.title: JWT payload has no account-type discriminator and LabUser is resolved before User

evidence.excerpt: _TokenUser and JWTClaims contain no account-kind field
build_token_payload emits user_id, lab_id, role and perm_ver only
citizen token payload uses user_id=citizen.id, lab_id=None, role=citizen, perm_ver=1
_extract_token accepts Bearer then cookie
get_current_user queries LabUser by user_id first, then User; token lab_id and role are not checked
perm_version is checked against whichever ORM class was selected

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Trace a token from login.py:186-193 into dependencies.py:77. Because User.id and LabUser.id are independent primary-key spaces, LabUser.id==N can be selected even when the token claims lab_id=None and role=citizen. Falsification requires a signed account_kind claim plus strict dependency validation and a mismatch-rejection test.
findings.root_cause: Token identity is a bare integer without a domain qualifier; identity resolution uses table precedence rather than an explicit account-kind contract.
findings.impact: A token minted for one account family can resolve to another account family on ID collision, potentially conferring lab roles, lab scope and permissions or misattributing audit and permission-version checks.
findings.remediation: Add a signed account_kind claim at issuance, validate it in every token-consuming dependency, enforce lab_id/workspace consistency with the resolved principal, and reject mismatches.
alternatives: Use globally unique ULIDs or UUIDs across account tables and still validate account_kind
Namespace the user_id claim as lab:<id> or user:<id>
findings.preferred_alternative: Globally unique identifiers plus explicit account_kind validation

findings.title: Privileged login checks MFA enrollment only and issues full tokens without an MFA challenge

evidence.excerpt: privileged roles check only mfa.has_mfa_enabled(user.id)
create_token and create_refresh_token are called immediately after enrollment check
tokens and session response are returned
setup_totp creates an active MFADevice before any verification
has_mfa_enabled only checks for an active device row
MFA verification endpoints depend on get_current_user, i.e. require an existing token

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Trace a privileged login through login.py:141-160 and confirm no call to verify_totp, complete_webauthn_authentication or verify_mfa_session before create_token at :197. Falsification requires a short-lived pre-token MFA session verified before full token issuance plus a password-only rejection test.
findings.root_cause: MFA is modeled as an enrollment attribute rather than a second authentication step in the login state machine.
findings.impact: Password compromise or phishing against a privileged account yields a fully authenticated session even when MFA is enrolled, creating false assurance of MFA enforcement.
findings.remediation: Implement staged privileged login: credential verification, scoped short-lived MFA challenge token, MFA verification, then full access and refresh token issuance; add replay, expiry and negative tests.
alternatives: Use WebAuthn as primary passwordless factor for privileged roles
Require step-up MFA at every critical API call via AuthorizationDecisionService
findings.preferred_alternative: Staged login plus step-up for critical actions

findings.title: Logout revokes only cookie tokens; Bearer clients retain usable sessions

evidence.excerpt: _extract_token accepts Bearer credentials before cookie
logout reads access token only from request.cookies
refresh token revocation reads only the cookie
perm_version bump depends on user_id which remains None for Bearer-only logout

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Compare dependencies.py:32-34 with login.py:258 and :270. A Bearer-only client has no cookies, so no JTI is blacklisted and no user_id is derived. Falsification requires logout to use the shared extraction helper and a test proving a Bearer token receives 401 after logout.
findings.root_cause: Token extraction logic is duplicated and inconsistent between request authentication and logout.
findings.impact: Logout is ineffective for native and mobile clients; retained or stolen tokens remain valid until expiry, defeating session termination and incident response.
findings.remediation: Reuse _extract_token in logout, accept both Bearer and cookie tokens, blacklist both JTIs, derive user_id from either source, and bump perm_version when identity is known.
alternatives: Server-side session store with explicit session IDs
Short access-token TTL with refresh-token rotation
findings.preferred_alternative: Shared token extraction plus both revocation layers and short TTL defense in depth

findings.title: Patient PHI routes require authentication but no per-action authorization or consent

evidence.excerpt: GET /patients depends only on get_current_user
POST /patients depends only on get_current_user and passes force_create through
family, children, read-by-id and update routes depend only on get_current_user
get_current_user authenticates and checks perm_version and lab-active state but performs no patient action authorization
stricter require_institutional_permission pattern exists but is not used by /patients

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Inspect each listed route signature and confirm absence of require_institutional_permission, require_niam_*, require_consent or AuthorizationDecisionService. Falsification requires explicit patient:read/manage/create dependencies plus negative tests for citizen and low-privilege actors.
findings.root_cause: get_current_user is used as a substitute for authorization; no per-resource policy is attached to the legacy patient surface.
findings.impact: Any authenticated account that can obtain a token may enumerate, read, create or update PHI without role, purpose or consent checks.
findings.remediation: Add explicit patient action permissions to every route, bind reads and writes to institutional workspace or facility scope, apply consent for cross-lab or citizen data, and add negative authorization tests.
alternatives: Wrap the legacy patient router in a policy-enforcing facade
Migrate to the Health Core authorized facade once it is actually wired
findings.preferred_alternative: Policy-enforcing facade now, Health Core migration as target state

findings.title: Adaptive-auth policy, MFA and session control plane is mounted authentication-only

evidence.excerpt: adaptive_auth router mounted with _AUTH_REQUIRED only
risk history readable for arbitrary account_id
MFA challenge creation and verification accept caller-supplied account_id and mfa_id
risk policies can be created and arbitrarily updated
session policies can be created and updated
session policy enforcement and expiry checks callable without authorization

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Follow router.py:61 into adaptive_auth/routes.py and confirm no role or permission dependency on listed handlers. Falsification requires explicit security-admin permission, actor/account binding, audit of mutations and negative tests.
findings.root_cause: Security-control configuration endpoints were treated as ordinary authenticated APIs.
findings.impact: Any authenticated identity can weaken risk thresholds, manipulate session policies, forge MFA challenges for other accounts and read risk history.
findings.remediation: Require a dedicated security-admin permission for all adaptive-auth reads and mutations, bind account_id to actor unless explicitly authorized, audit every change, and add negative tests.
alternatives: Move endpoints under the NIAM admin router with _require_permission
Make endpoints internal-only and remove from the public API
findings.preferred_alternative: Move under NIAM admin with dedicated permission keys

findings.title: Async NIAM actor dependency omits the account-lock check present in the sync dependency

evidence.excerpt: sync actor query includes Account.is_locked.is_(False) at line 54
async actor query filters status and is_active but omits is_locked
generic resolver checks is_locked and locked_until but async workspace actor path does not call it
_AUTH_REQUIRED uses get_current_niam_actor, the async variant

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Diff the two queries at workspaces.py:47-58 and :75-85 and confirm is_locked appears only in the sync variant. Falsification requires the async query to include an equivalent fail-closed lock predicate and a locked-account negative test.
findings.root_cause: Duplicated authentication logic drifted between sync and async implementations.
findings.impact: A locked NIAM account can continue to access all async NIAM routes, including the affected control planes, until token expiry or separate revocation.
findings.remediation: Consolidate both dependencies on one canonical predicate builder that always checks active status, is_active, is_locked, valid session and JTI revocation; add parity tests.
alternatives: Add the missing predicate directly as a hotfix
Replace both dependencies with a shared account and session validator
findings.preferred_alternative: Shared validator, with direct predicate addition as immediate hotfix

findings.title: Health Core deny-by-default authorization facade is not wired into runtime routes

evidence.excerpt: module docstring explicitly states nothing is wired into a route or factory.py
AuthorizedHealthCore is described as the authorization gate callers must use
facade is exported
representative route mounting block contains no AuthorizedHealthCore integration

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Read guard.py:3-4 and search factory and route modules for AuthorizedHealthCore; no runtime consumer was found. Falsification requires a composition root that routes clinical and lab reads and mutations exclusively through the facade plus bypass-prevention tests.
findings.root_cause: A strong authorization component was delivered as a library without a composition-root integration step.
findings.impact: The deny-by-default policy engine, scope index and audited authorization decisions are not applied to HTTP traffic; any claim based on this facade is NOT IMPLEMENTED at runtime.
findings.remediation: Wire the facade into the clinical gateway composition root, replace direct unwrapped service calls, and add route-level and architecture tests preventing bypass imports.
alternatives: Keep facade dormant and explicitly exclude it from security claims
Expose it through a thin FastAPI dependency wrapper
Migrate routes to the canonical clinical gateway
findings.preferred_alternative: Migrate routes to canonical clinical gateway with a thin wrapper as transition

findings.title: Security-relevant fixes and evidence remain uncommitted; release evidence is internally inconsistent

evidence.excerpt: HOLD - do not release to production
S-01..S-13 and kill-switch fixes implemented in working tree; uncommitted and not yet independently reviewed
authorization coverage REMEDIATED (uncommitted, unreviewed); security certification NOT CERTIFIED; release candidate HOLD
DEP-AUDIT-BACKEND set to VERIFIED in uncommitted addendum
addendum states it does not certify production readiness or clinical safety; release remains HOLD
uncommitted VITE_API_BASE_URL changed to https://api.gula-platform.org/api

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Read-only git status at HEAD 2206654 showed large modified and untracked security-relevant sets including config.py, factory.py, login.py, all health_core, NIAM control planes and dependency manifests. Falsification requires a clean committed tree at a named revision containing all fixes, regenerated gates and a consistent decision record.
findings.root_cause: Remediation evidence was written into governance reports before the corresponding code was committed and independently reviewed.
findings.impact: A release evaluator cannot reproduce the certified state from HEAD; changes can be lost or deployed selectively; assurance claims cannot be tied to an immutable revision.
findings.remediation: Commit the complete reviewed change-set atomically, rerun all gates against that commit, update decision records with the exact commit hash, and reconcile VERIFIED dependency language with the still-HOLD release decision.
alternatives: Revert uncommitted security changes and reapply under review
Create a signed evidence bundle bound to the working tree for internal testing only
findings.preferred_alternative: Atomic reviewed commit with gates rerun at that revision

findings.title: Cross-facility PHI disclosure in national-ID duplicate response

evidence.excerpt: _check_duplicates receives lab_id but the national-ID branch queries Patient.national_id_hash == nid_hash without a lab filter and returns patient_to_dict(existing)
patient_to_dict exposes full_name, phone, birth_date, gender, email, health_id, is_minor, guardian_id and created_at
route passes caller lab_id and returns service error body, including existing_patient
composite index ix_patients_lab_nid over lab_id and national_id_hash shows intended tenant-partitioned lookup

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Inspect patient_service.py:334-345 and compare with the phone branch at :347-350; the national-ID query lacks the tenant predicate and the 409 body carries the full patient DTO. Falsification requires a lab-scoped query plus a non-identifying conflict marker or an explicitly authorized MPI disclosure path.
findings.root_cause: MPI-style global identity lookup was implemented inside a lab-scoped patient-creation path without tenant isolation or purpose limitation on the response.
findings.impact: A user at one facility who knows a national ID can receive another facility's patient PHI including name, phone, DOB, gender, email, health ID and guardian link.
findings.remediation: Scope duplicate query by lab_id for local duplicates; route national cross-facility matches through the MPI consent and authorization layer; return only a conflict token; add cross-facility negative tests.
alternatives: Keep global duplicate detection but return exists:true only
Require an explicit audited MPI disclosure permission and log purpose
findings.preferred_alternative: Non-identifying conflict marker on create endpoint; dedicated MPI API for authorized disclosure

findings.title: Consent enforcement is effectively unwired and break-glass is a client-supplied header

evidence.excerpt: require_consent implements owner, emergency and active-consent checks
break-glass flag is read from X-Emergency-Access header
doctor role plus header is allowed with only an audit row; no justification, approval or expiry
owner bypass relies on attached citizen_ulid attribute not directly exposed by LabUser until portal fully live
only production use found: GET /mpi/citizens/{citizen_ulid}/access with Depends(require_consent(read:citizen))
patient PHI routes do not use consent

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Read-only usage scan found require_consent only in its definition, mpi/api.py:571 and tests. Falsification requires consent dependencies on all PHI reads plus server-issued break-glass grants with case ID, justification, expiry and post-use approval.
findings.root_cause: The consent engine was built as a reusable dependency but not adopted by primary PHI surfaces; break-glass was modeled as a request flag rather than a governed clinical process.
findings.impact: Most PHI access is not consent-gated; where consent is used, a doctor can self-authorize emergency access by setting a header, producing only an after-the-fact audit record.
findings.remediation: Apply require_consent to every cross-lab or citizen PHI read; replace raw header with short-lived server-issued emergency grant tied to case and approver; require post-use review; add tests for denied, consented, owner and emergency paths.
alternatives: Move break-glass into the clinical gateway policy engine with purpose-of-use context
Require signed emergency token plus mandatory review queue while retaining header
findings.preferred_alternative: Clinical gateway policy engine with governed emergency grants

findings.title: Client-controlled force_create bypasses duplicate detection without authorization

evidence.excerpt: force_create: bool = False with comment skip duplicate check
force_create passed directly into create_patient
duplicate detection skipped entirely when force_create is true
national_id_hash is indexed but not unique
MPI resolution still runs after the bypass

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Trace force_create from routes/patients.py:39,199 into patient_service.py:149-155 and confirm no permission check and no uniqueness constraint. Falsification requires an authorized override with mandatory reason and audit plus a transaction-safe uniqueness or MPI merge path.
findings.root_cause: A clinical safety override was exposed as an ordinary request parameter without authority, justification or compensation.
findings.impact: Duplicate patient rows can fragment identity, duplicate orders and results, and increase wrong-patient clinical risk.
findings.remediation: Remove the public flag; implement a server-side override permission with mandatory reason and audit; add a partial unique constraint or transaction-safe lock; require duplicate-resolution review.
alternatives: Keep override only in an admin-only endpoint
Automatically route duplicates to MPI review instead of creating a row
findings.preferred_alternative: Automatic MPI review with controlled admin override only

findings.title: Raw PII is written into the tamper-evident audit log

evidence.excerpt: audit details string includes patient.full_name and phone
log_action serializes details and writes it verbatim into AuditLog.details
audit immutability and tenant-context hash-chain are owner-listed controls that must be preserved

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Read patient_service.py:194 and audit_service.py:198-212 and confirm raw name and phone are stored. Falsification requires redaction or tokenization at the logging boundary and a test asserting no raw PII in AuditLog.details.
findings.root_cause: Audit logging treats details as free-form human text rather than a data-minimized structured field.
findings.impact: The append-only audit log becomes a secondary PHI repository with different retention and access controls, complicating minimization and breach response.
findings.remediation: Log resource IDs, reference tokens and field names only; never log raw names, phones, emails, national IDs or family IDs; add a redaction helper and CI PII-pattern test.
alternatives: Store a salted reference token for the patient
Encrypt audit details with a separate key and strict reviewer permission
findings.preferred_alternative: Reference token plus minimization; encryption only as defense in depth

findings.title: Minor and guardian linkage is optional and unenforced

evidence.excerpt: guardian_id described as strongly recommended for under-18 patients, not required
guardian validated only if guardian_id is not None; no age-derived requirement
guardian FK is nullable and is_minor is derived from birth_date
children view returns patients linked by guardian_id; missing links silently reduce visibility

findings.safe_reproduction_or_falsification: Compare age derivation in models/patient.py:54-59 with create validation in patient_service.py:157-163 and confirm a minor can be submitted with guardian_id=None. Falsification requires a validator requiring an adult guardian for minors plus tests for missing, invalid, cross-lab and deceased guardian cases.
findings.root_cause: Guardian linkage is treated as optional metadata rather than as a privacy and safety control for pediatric records.
findings.impact: Minor PHI can be created without a verifiable guardian, breaking consent and guardian-authorization assumptions and weakening auditability of who may act for the child.
findings.remediation: Derive age from birth_date, require a guardian for minors, verify guardian is an adult in the same lab or facility scope, and record guardian IDs only in audit details.
alternatives: Block creation until guardian verification
Create a pending state with limited access until guardian link is supplied
findings.preferred_alternative: Pending state for emergency intake; block routine registration without guardian
